card.name: Occlusion and enclosed-space wording
card.fires_on: The word occlusive (or its start, oc) in warnings about covering a skin product with dressings, and the word enclosed in 'enclosed space' for smoke or fumes. It also fires on 'accumulation' after 'drug'.

modes.label: Occlusive dressings
modes.description: Pieces of the word occlusive/occlusion in topical steroid warnings about covered skin.
modes.example: Do not use with oc<<clusive>> dressings unless directed by a physician.

modes.label: Enclosed space
modes.description: The word enclosed describing a closed area where smoke or exhaust was breathed in.
modes.example: Exposure to fire or smoke in an<< enclosed>> area Presence of soot around the mouth

modes.label: Drug build-up
modes.description: The word accumulation after drug, about substances building up in the body.
modes.example: adjusted according to creatinine clearance rates to prevent drug<< accumulation>>.

card.writes: It pushes toward words about being shut in, trapped or retained, such as retention, trapped and trapping.
card.plain: It marks text about things being covered, sealed in or building up, like occlusive dressings or smoke in a closed room.
